title: Using Pre-Training Can Improve Model Robustness and Uncertainty
publication_status_observed: Proceedings of the 36th ICML, Long Beach, California, PMLR 97, 2019; arXiv preprint arXiv:1901.09960v5
main_claims: Pre-training on a large related dataset substantially improves model robustness to adversarial perturbations, label corruption, and class imbalance, even when it does not improve clean accuracy.
Adversarial pre-training (pre-training with untargeted adversarial examples) improves adversarial robustness by approximately 10% absolute over prior state-of-the-art.
Pre-training significantly improves confidence calibration and out-of-distribution detection, often by more than halving the calibration error.
methodology: Wide ResNet models are pre-trained on Downsampled ImageNet (32x32), then fine-tuned on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. The paper tests robustness under adversarial perturbations (PGD), label corruption (forward correction, GLC), class imbalance, OOD detection (AUROC/AUPR), and calibration (RMS/MAD). Comparisons are made against training-from-scratch baselines and task-specific robustness methods.
key_results: Adversarial pre-training + fine-tuning achieves 57.4% adversarial accuracy on CIFAR-10 vs 45.8% for adversarial training from scratch.
Pre-training with no correction achieves AUC of 15.9% on CIFAR-10 label corruption, surpassing Forward Correction (25.5%) without pre-training.
RMS calibration error reduced by more than half on all datasets with pre-training (e.g., CIFAR-100: 13.3% → 3.6%).
limitations: Pre-training benefits are specific to scenarios where diverse unlabeled data is available for pre-training.
The mechanism by which pre-training improves robustness and calibration is not fully characterized.
Experiments use 32x32 Downsampled ImageNet; the findings may not transfer to all architectures and scales.
relevance_to_rq: Tangentially relevant to the ood_benchmarks sub-topic: demonstrates that representation quality (from pre-training) improves robustness and calibration under distribution shift, motivating the study of representation stability as a driver of OOD accuracy — aligned with the RQ's CKA stability hypothesis. However, the paper does not involve SAM or flatness measures.
